title: The one who would be a steward
hook: Allah tells the angels He will place a steward on the earth, and they ask why (2:30)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the end of camp one: juz' 'amma, the short surahs. Your line was the ones every Muslim child knows. Did you read al-'Asr? Today, camp two, the stories. Day twenty-two.
screen: `JUZ' 'AMMA — THE ONES EVERY MUSLIM CHILD KNOWS.`

segments.voice: Camp two begins, and the path changes shape. For the next weeks, it's stories: the prophets, one after another, Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Yusuf, Maryam and Isa, and then the Prophet himself, peace be upon him. Told in words only, the way the Qur'an tells them. And the first story doesn't start on earth at all. It starts in a conversation. God speaks to the angels, who in this verse describe themselves as hymning His praise, and tells them a plan. Something new is coming. And the angels do something surprising. They ask a question.
screen: `CAMP TWO: THE STORIES.` → `A CONVERSATION WITH THE ANGELS.` → `AND THE ANGELS ASK WHY.`

segments.voice: Here's the verse, surah two, verse thirty. God says to the angels, in Pickthall's words: “Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth.” Viceroy is Pickthall's choice. The Arabic is khalifah, and translators wrestle with it: viceroy, deputy, successor, steward. The root, kh-l-f, means to come after, to stand in for. A khalifah is someone who holds a place on another's behalf. Not the owner. The one entrusted. The later word caliph comes from it, but here it's about every human being. And the angels answer. Paraphrasing: will You place there someone who will spread corruption and shed blood, while we praise You and call You holy? Commentators are careful here: this was a question, not an objection. They wanted to understand. How could something that dangerous be the one put in charge? And God doesn't strike them down for asking. He answers, in Pickthall's words: “Surely I know that which ye know not.” That's all, for now. Tomorrow the story shows them what He meant. But notice what this first scene sets up. Human beings enter the story as a risk, and a trust at the same time. Capable of bloodshed. Handed the earth anyway, to look after. And the first thing that happens, before anyone has done anything, is an honest question, asked out loud, to God, and answered.
screen: `I AM ABOUT TO PLACE A VICEROY.` · `KHALIFAH — ONE WHO STANDS IN FOR.` · `THE ANGELS ASK WHY.` · `I KNOW WHAT YOU KNOW NOT.` · then, large: `EVEN THE ANGELS ASKED.`

segments.voice: The bell will give you two minutes. Sit comfortably. Let one real question come up, one you've been carrying about your life, or the world, or God. Not a rhetorical one. A real one, the kind you'd feel a little shy asking out loud. Let it come in plain words. Then just sit with it. You don't have to answer it. In the story, even the angels asked, and nobody was punished for it. If you pray, you can ask it there. If you don't, just hold it in the open, and let it breathe. The bell holds the time.
Khalifah. A steward, a deputy, one who stands in for another. The Qur'an's word, in this scene, for what a human being is here to be.
Your line: even the angels asked. Today, ask one honest question you've been holding back, at work, at home, anywhere. Ask it kindly, and listen to the answer. Day twenty-two.

howItsDone: Many Muslims understand being a khalifah on the earth as a trust: caring for creation and for one another as stewards answerable to God, and Friday sermons often return to this verse.

original.note: Arabic: steward, deputy, successor, from kh-l-f, to come after; the source of the English word caliph.

trapdoor: what you thought: khalifah means caliph, a ruler.
what it means: khalifah — a steward, one who holds the earth on another's behalf; in 2:30, every human being.
what a scholar hears: kh-l-f, to succeed or stand in for; commentators differ whether humans succeed earlier beings on the earth or stand in for God's will as trustees; Pickthall chose viceroy.

Surely I know that which ye know not.

sources.ref: Qur'an 6:165 (humans placed as successors on the earth)

notes: Pickthall 2:30 quoted from memory: 'And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not.' The angels' words are paraphrased in the script. Confirm.

Meanings of khalifah: commentators differ (successor to earlier inhabitants such as jinn; successors of one another; vicegerent/trustee of God). Some scholars object to 'God's deputy' as a phrase. The script uses 'one who stands in for another' and 'steward'. Confirm.
'Angels don't rebel in the Qur'an': the mainstream view (66:6, 21:27); Iblis's status (angel or jinn) is taken up on day 24.
Camp two opening is in the review and hook: the stories of the prophets, told in words only, ending with the Prophet ﷺ.
